Released: 20 August 2026

EDB Postgres Distributed (PGD) 5.9.5 includes only bug fixes focused on improving stability and reliability. For a list of known issues, see [Known issues](/pgd/current/known_issues/).

## Bug Fixes

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Version</th><th>Description</th><th width="10%">Addresses</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Fixed node-join failure caused by an under-sized replication origin estimate during catch-up.</summary><hr/><p>The function <code>bdr.get_min_required_replication_slots()</code> previously ignored the temporary catch-up subscription active during a node join, so joining a cluster sized to the reported minimum exhausted <code>max_replication_slots</code> and failed. The estimate now accounts for the catch-up subscription, and a new <code>bdr.get_min_required_active_replication_origins()</code> function returns the matching estimate for PostgreSQL 18's separate <code>max_active_replication_origins</code> limit.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Fixed a crash caused by a race between a joining and a parting node.</summary><hr/><p>A joining node sometimes reached the <code>PART_CATCHUP</code> phase of a concurrent node part before it had created a replication origin for the parting node, crashing the manager or writer process when it tried to access the missing origin. PGD now creates the origin in this case, and removes it automatically once the parting node reaches the <code>PARTED</code> state.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Fixed a crash on dynamic partition creation for <code>HASH</code> and <code>LIST</code> subpartitions.</summary><hr/><p>Creating a dynamic interval partition with <code>HASH</code> or <code>LIST</code> subpartitions crashed the originating node, and once fixed, produced duplicate partition names that looped until the server ran out of memory. The partition-naming hook is now strategy-aware, producing a unique, deterministic name for each partition across all nodes.</p>
</details></td><td>61769</td></tr>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Fixed resource leaks in <code>bdr.ri_fkey_on_del_trigger</code>.</summary><hr/><p>The <code>bdr.ri_fkey_on_del_trigger</code> trigger function left a relation, a tuple descriptor, and a snapshot open every time it ran, logging <code>resource was not closed</code> warnings on every node. The function now closes these resources correctly.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>
